sections.h2: Ways to sell in Palm Coast
sections.html:
An owner in Palm Coast can take a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell as is. Many homes here draw interest for canal frontage, trails and a retiree-friendly layout.

The city covers 95.36 square miles of land, so conditions differ by neighborhood. Canal homes, trail-side homes and newer subdivisions each draw different buyers. A seller who knows which group fits the property can choose between a canal-focused listing and a quick sale to someone who handles the repairs. The city has 39,807 households with an average of 2.46 people, so buyers are often couples or small families.

Palm Coast is a young city on Florida's northeast coast, incorporated in 1999. It has 70 miles of saltwater and freshwater canals, the Intracoastal Waterway and more than 130 miles of connecting trails. Water access is what many buyers look for first, so describe it clearly in your listing.

Useful numbers: Building Services at 386-986-3780 and Code Compliance at 386-986-3764. The city's Departments menu includes a lien request form and a garage sale permit page, both handy for a seller clearing out a house. City Council meets on the first Tuesday of each month at 6:00 p.m. and the third Tuesday at 9 a.m., at City Hall, 160 Lake Avenue.

Growth here has been fast and retirees make up a large share of residents. The 2020 count was 89,258 people, up from 75,180 in 2010.

Household income sits near $77,350, so many sellers here are on retirement income.

More work needs a permit than many owners assume. Florida Building Code section 105.1 covers construction, alterations, repairs, re-roofs and work on electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems.

  • Pergolas, gazebos, decks, detached patio covers and greenhouses are residential accessory structures and need a permit.
  • The city uses a design wind speed of 120 miles per hour, and a pre-manufactured structure must be engineered for that figure.
  • Applications go through the online permit portal, and accessory structure review is usually done in 3 to 5 business days.
  • A permit stays active six months from issue. If it lapses without the required inspections, a new permit is required.
  • A foundation survey may be required before vertical construction.

Added a deck or a screened room? Make sure the permit was closed. An inspector or title company can catch an open one, and fixing it before listing is cheaper than doing it mid-contract.

Flagler County sets your value as of January 1 and mails the bill in November. Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax, and the bill is normally prorated with the buyer at the closing table. Value comes from the Property Appraiser and the bill from the Tax Collector.

  • File for homestead by March 1. The exemption has two layers: the first $25,000 applies to every tax, and a second layer of up to $25,000 comes off the non-school taxes only, on value above $50,000.
  • Pay the whole bill in November for a 4 percent discount, which shrinks to 1 percent by February.
  • Assessments on non-homestead property are capped at a 10 percent yearly increase.
  • Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

Call the county property appraiser if you are unsure which exemption currently applies to you.

The stamp tax on a deed is $0.70 for every $100 of price, which is the state rate, and the clerk takes it when the deed is filed. The clerk adds its own charges: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each page after, $1.00 for every name past four, and a technology charge of $4 per page.

A quitclaim deed is taxed too. A lady bird deed, though, was found by a Department of Revenue advisement to pass no present beneficial interest on the facts presented, so it drew no stamp tax. The closing agent adds up the real figures.

Inheritance sales begin at the clerk's probate file. Because about 29.5% of residents are 65 or older, they come up often here. A small estate of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets, or one where the death was over two years ago, can use summary administration. Creditors lose their claims after the later of three months from first notice publication or thirty days from service on a required creditor.

If someone is living in the house without permission, the sheriff can act on a verified complaint, but only where there is no tenancy, no family tie and no pending lawsuit. A claim of adverse possession needs seven years of possession plus tax payments and a return filed with the property appraiser, and living in a home on that claim before filing is trespass. A month-to-month tenant is different and gets 30 days' notice before a monthly period ends.

• Permit records: call Building Services at 386-986-3780 and confirm that decks, pergolas, roofs and screened structures were closed out. Remember that a permit expires after six months without inspections.
  • City liens and code issues: use the lien request form in the Departments menu, and reach Code Compliance at 386-986-3764.
  • Utility account: the Customer Service line, 386-986-2360, handles billing and new service, so schedule the change for closing day.
  • Garage sale: the city has a garage sales page if you plan to clear out belongings before moving.
  • Homestead paperwork: keep your exemption records so you can use portability if you buy another Florida home within three years.

You do not need all of it before a cash offer, but every item you finish trims days off the closing.

Once the contract is signed, a title search looks for liens and unpaid taxes while the closing agent drafts the deed and settlement statement. A cash deal has no lender appraisal, so title work and any open permit or lien set the schedule. A missing document is the usual cause of a slipped closing, so answer calls from the agent promptly.

Plan the move too. Book movers for a day or two after closing in case the date shifts, and leave openers, keys and any warranties for the buyer. If you have a canal dock or seawall, hand over whatever records you have on it, since waterfront buyers ask about both. Ask the agent how and when your proceeds arrive, and file the signed settlement statement with your tax records.

faqs.q: When did Palm Coast become a city?
faqs.a: It incorporated in 1999. It sits along canals and the Intracoastal Waterway in Flagler County.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a deck or pergola?
faqs.a: Yes. Pergolas, gazebos, decks and detached patio covers are accessory structures that require a permit under the Florida Building Code.

faqs.q: What wind speed does the city use for design?
faqs.a: 120 miles per hour. A pre-manufactured structure should carry a Florida engineer's signed and sealed plans for that speed before you buy it.

faqs.q: How long does a Palm Coast building permit stay active?
faqs.a: Six months from issue. If it expires without the required inspections, a new permit is needed.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate in Flagler County?
faqs.a: $0.70 per $100 of price, collected by the clerk as the deed is filed.
